column1: If you resist change, you resist life.
column3: What is a change you fought hard against that turned out to be good for you?
column4: What finally helped you stop resisting it?

column1: The most beautiful moments in life are moments when you are expressing your joy, not when you are seeking it.
column3: When did you last feel joy simply pouring out of you?
column4: What were you doing and who was there with you?

column1: Learning to listen is the essence of intelligent living.
column3: Who in your life makes you feel truly listened to?
column4: What do they do that others miss?

column1: When pain, misery, or anger happen, it is time to look within you, not around you.
column3: When something upsets you what is your first instinct about where to look for the cause?
column4: What have you learned about yourself from looking inward instead?

column1: Reactivity is enslavement. Responsibility is freedom.
column3: What is a situation where you reacted in the moment and later wished you had paused?
column4: What would responding instead of reacting have looked like that time?

column1: Unless you do the right things, the right things will not happen to you.
column3: What is something good in your life that came from steady right action rather than luck?
column4: Which small habit made the biggest difference?

column1: If instead of trying to manage your time, you clearly set your Priorities, time will arrange itself around them.
column3: What are the two or three priorities you would want your days to arrange themselves around?
column4: What usually crowds them out and how do you push back?

column1: If bitter experiences happen in your life, the Choice is this – you can either become wise or wounded.
column3: What is a painful experience that ended up making you wiser?
column4: What did it take to turn that wound into wisdom?

column1: Do not waste your life comparing yourself to others. Just see if you are one notch better than you were yesterday.
column3: Who do you most often find yourself comparing yourself to?
column4: What would being one notch better than yesterday look like for you this week?

column1: Most people in the world are not busy – they are just preoccupied.
column3: What keeps your mind preoccupied even when you are not actually busy?
column4: What helps you set it down and be present?

column1: The closest and dearest in your life get the worst of you. No stranger on the street gets such a nasty deal.
column3: Who sees the worst of you simply because they are closest to you?
column4: What could you offer them that you usually save for strangers?

column1: What you do should not define who you are. Who you are should define what you do.
column3: How would you describe who you are without mentioning your job?
column4: How does that inner self show up in the work you do?

column1: Very few people are Living their lives. The rest are just making a living.
column3: When do you feel most fully alive rather than just getting through the day?
column4: What would it take to have more of those moments?

column1: People always try to meet the most wonderful person in the world. Why not be that wonderful person yourself.
column3: What quality do you admire in others that you would most like to grow in yourself?
column4: What is one small step toward being that kind of person?

column1: For someone who is Joyful, life is brief. For someone who is miserable, it is bloody long.
column3: When has time flown by because you were so happy?
column4: What made that stretch of life feel so light?

column1: People are not here to be used. People are here to be loved and shared with. Things are for use – not people.
column3: Who in your life makes you feel genuinely valued as a person?
column4: How do you try to pass that feeling on to others?

column1: A spouse is not a destination but a fellow traveler.
column3: What has a long relationship taught you about travelling alongside someone?
column4: What do you most appreciate about the people who walk beside you?

column1: Trust does not mean that others have to do things the way you expect them to. Trust means being consciously vulnerable.
column3: Who have you trusted even when they did things differently than you would?
column4: What did that trust ask of you?

column1: The same problem recurring means you are the problem.
column3: What problem keeps showing up in your life in different forms?
column4: What part might you be playing in it?

column1: Do not save your Joy for later. When you are joyful, your whole life is a celebration.
column3: What is a joy you have been putting off for some future day?
column4: What would it look like to enjoy it now?

column1: What is a friend? A friend is another confused human being like you. If the two of you can be with each other sincerely, that is when real friendship happens.
column3: Who is a friend you can be your honest and confused self with?
column4: How did that friendship become so real?

column1: If who you are is clearly established within yourself, what people say will not matter.
column3: When have you felt secure enough in yourself that criticism barely touched you?
column4: Where did that steadiness come from?

column1: Life is not about What you do. It is all about How you do it.
column3: What is an ordinary task you take real pride in doing well?
column4: What does doing it with care give back to you?

column1: If you maintain Exuberance of energy, freshness of mind, and a loving heart, every day is a new adventure.
column3: When did a day last feel like a real adventure to you?
column4: What helps you keep a fresh mind and a loving heart?

column1: When people give advice, always look at whether it has worked for them.
column3: What is the best piece of advice you have ever received?
column4: How had it worked in the life of the person who gave it?

column1: To be committed to each other beyond success and failure, health and ill-health, life and death – that is what makes you a Family.
column3: Who has stuck by you through both good and hard times?
column4: What did their loyalty mean to you then and now?

column1: No work is stressful. It is your inability to manage your body, mind, and emotions that makes it stressful.
column3: What part of your work tends to feel most stressful?
column4: What helps you handle it with a steadier body and mind?

column1: Every day, you are gifted with a glorious sunrise and a glorious sunset. Life is happening. You are alive. What more do you want.
column3: What simple everyday moment makes you feel glad to be alive?
column4: How could you make more room for moments like that?

column1: There are two kinds of people: those who make things happen, and those who enjoy it when it happens well, and complain when it does not.
column3: When have you been the one who made something happen instead of waiting for it?
column4: What pushed you to step up that time?

column1: People irritate you simply because they are not the way you expect or want them to be. Essentially, they are not like you.
column3: What kind of person tends to irritate you most?
column4: What might that irritation reveal about your own expectations?

column1: One thing every human being can strive for is to leave this world a little better than it was when you entered it.
column3: What is one way you hope to leave the world a little better?
column4: Who first showed you what that kind of contribution looks like?

column1: One moment of absolute gratitude can transform your whole life.
column3: What is something you are deeply grateful for that you rarely mention?
column4: How has that gratitude shaped the way you live?

column1: With enough attention, just about anything can be mastered.
column3: What skill have you mastered simply by paying close attention over time?
column4: What would you love to give that kind of attention to next?

column1: Fear and anxiety are consequences of your imagination running wild. You are suffering a situation that may never happen.
column3: What worry have you carried that never actually came true?
column4: What helps you rein in your imagination when it runs ahead?

column1: Recognize people around you for the best that you have seen in them. In recognizing the best instead of the worst, you will kindle, nurture, and receive the best of everyone.
column3: Who brings out the best in you by seeing the best in you?
column4: Whose best could you start recognizing more often?

column1: Do not hold back your love, your joy, and your exuberance. Only what you give becomes your quality, not what you hold back.
column3: What is something you tend to hold back that you would like to give more freely?
column4: What makes it feel risky to let it out?

column1: Do not worry about your future. Do your present well, and the future will blossom.
column3: What part of your future do you worry about most right now?
column4: What could you do well today that would serve that future?

column1: To forgive does not mean to forget. To forgive means not to carry any bitterness in you because that destroys your life.
column3: What is something you have forgiven without forgetting?
column4: How did letting go of the bitterness change things for you?

column1: Happiness starts with you – not with your relationships, job, or money.
column3: Where in your life have you found happiness that did not depend on people or things?
column4: How do you return to that place on a hard day?

column1: Whoever you meet, speak to them like it is the last time you may have that opportunity. It will transform your life.
column3: Who is someone you wish you had said more to while you had the chance?
column4: How has that changed the way you talk to people now?

column1: When there are troubles within us, we must address them head-on. Do not look for distractions – distraction is not a solution.
column3: What distraction do you reach for when something is bothering you?
column4: What has helped you face a problem head-on instead?

column1: Competitors are not enemies. They are people who keep reminding you of your own shortcomings. Your quality control.
column3: Who is a rival or competitor who made you better?
column4: What shortcoming did they help you see in yourself?

column1: Whether you have anger, hatred, jealousy, or resentment against someone, essentially, it only works against you.
column3: What is a grudge or resentment you once held that ended up hurting mostly you?
column4: What helped you finally put it down?

column1: For a committed person, there is no such thing as failure – just lessons to be learnt on the way.
column3: What failure turned out to be one of your best lessons?
column4: What did it teach you that success never could?

column1: How much money you make only determines comfort, never the quality of your life.
column3: What did you learn about money and comfort versus a good life?
column4: What matters most to the quality of your days that money cannot buy?

column1: A love affair need not be with any particular person. You could have a great love affair with life itself.
column3: What part of life are you most in love with right now?
column4: How did that love first begin for you?

column1: Whatever you do, you can either do it willingly or unwillingly. If you do it willingly, it will be heaven. If you do it unwillingly, it will be hell.
column3: What is a task you once did grudgingly that later became a pleasure?
column4: What shifted in your attitude toward it?

column1: There is no need to do what others are doing. You must do what truly matters to you.
column3: What is something that truly matters to you even though others do not pursue it?
column4: What keeps you committed to it?

column1: Once your relationships are about sharing your Joy, rather than extracting Joy out of someone else, you will have wonderful relationships with anyone.
column3: How do you share your joy with the people closest to you?
column4: What changes in a relationship when both people come to give rather than get?

column1: What the world throws at you is not always in your hands. What you make of it is one hundred percent in your hands.
column3: What hard situation in your life did you turn into something good?
column4: What helped you decide how to respond to it?

column1: Youthfulness is not a question of years but a sense of Aliveness and Involvement.
column3: Who is the most youthful person you know regardless of their age?
column4: What keeps their spirit so alive and involved?

column1: What truly matters is not that people love you but that you are Loving.
column3: Who taught you what it means to be a loving person?
column4: How do you most like to show love to others?
